pack.title: Dinner-table interrogations
pack.description: Holiday cross-examination with witnesses. Loving, brief, final.

scenarios.setting: Holiday dinner. Your aunt, passing the potatoes, loud enough for all.
scenarios.jab: So are you seeing anyone, or still too picky?

replies.line: Still picky. It's working out great.
replies.why: Owning the label with a smile closes the topic in front of everyone.
A status plus a redirect ends testimony and restarts dinner.

replies.line: You'll be the first to know — now tell me about your trip.
replies.why: A promise plus a question about her trades interrogation for conversation.

replies.line: My love life has a press office now. It declines to comment.
replies.why: Absurd bureaucracy makes the question funny, which makes pursuing it awkward.
It reframes single life as a production, which the table laughs with.

trap.line: God, can we have ONE dinner without the inquisition?
trap.why: Snapping at the table makes you the scene instead of ending one.

scenarios.setting: Sunday dinner. Your father, carving, without looking up.
scenarios.jab: When are you going to get a real job?

replies.line: I have one. It pays for this wine.
replies.why: A fact plus a toast proves the point without arguing it.
replies.delivery: Raise your glass on the second sentence. Mean it.

replies.why: The Dad at the end keeps it family while the sentence stays final.

replies.line: It's real, I promise — want the two-minute version of what I do?
replies.why: Offering the explainer assumes curiosity instead of contempt, which invites him in.

replies.line: About the time carving counts as quality time.
replies.why: It answers a dig with a dig, which feels great for four seconds at family dinner.

replies.line: It's so real it pays taxes.
replies.why: Citing the IRS as your character witness ends the trial with proof.

trap.line: You have NO idea what I do. None.
trap.why: Correcting him with contempt turns dinner into the trial he's already holding.

scenarios.setting: Dinner at your in-laws. Your mother-in-law, serving you extra.
scenarios.jab: You look thin. Are you eating properly at home?

replies.line: I'm well fed. But I'll never refuse this cooking.
replies.why: It answers the worry and compliments the cook, ending the exam deliciously.

replies.line: Your cooking is the highlight of my meal plan.
replies.why: Making her the solution to the problem she raised dissolves it completely.

replies.line: I'm saving room. Strategically. For seconds.
replies.why: Treating thinness as tactics makes the whole table co-conspirators.
It answers the worry with an appetite, which is what she wanted to hear.
